messages.subject: Re: Please describe the featureCounts summary
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

I asked Wei about contributing. This was his reply:
>
> I’m not sure if it is a good idea to allow other people to make contributions to our package at the moment since the pacakge includes quite a few programs and it has a complexed structure. We might move the code repository to for example git-hub in the future, but at this stage we would like to keep it to ourselves to ensure a smooth development of the programs (especially new programs and algorithms).

I believe that source code for scientific software — regardless of complexity — should be stored in a permanent public repository that encourages contributions from the community.

I am also willing to help implement additional features or write more documentation. Github is an appropriate solution for managing contributions from the community.

Wei, I encourage you to look at the way other complex packages with multiple programs are organized on github:
https://github.com/samtools/samtools
https://github.com/lh3/seqtk

You might consider creating a separate github repo with the R package for subread.

Kamil

messages.subject: ERROR: BAM GZIP FORMAT ERROR.
messages.body_plain:
Hey,

I was running into a somewhat strange error in a subset of my BAM files that was occurring while running featureCounts. For maybe 10% of the samples, I would get this error message, which was more like a warning since the program did not stop running:

|| Process BAM file /dcs01/ajaffe/Brain/Hippo_Ribozero/BAM/HIPPO_Ribozero ... ||
||    Assign reads to features...                                             ||
ERROR: BAM GZIP FORMAT ERROR.
||    Total number of reads is : 42787041                                     ||
||    Number of successfully assigned reads is : 18873505 (44.1%)             ||
||    Running time : 1.44 minutes

This resulted in genes on some chromosomes not receiving any counts even though there were reads in the BAM file on those chromosomes - I've attached a file showing the seeming randomness of the missingness by chromosome

Any ideas whats causing this error? I tried reindexing the BAM files using samtools and have no issues opening any of the BAM files with missingness in samtools

Thanks,
Andrew

messages.subject: Re: ERROR: BAM GZIP FORMAT ERROR.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

Thank you for using featureCounts and providing us the very important feedback!

It is uncommon to see the "GZIP FORMAT ERROR" message from featureCounts; we have never seen such error messages in our pipelines. This error message is only reported when a compressed block in the BAM file is damaged, and that the gzip library cannot decompress it. When this error message is reported, the remaining part of the BAM file is skipped. The "total number of reads" reported by featureCounts is the number of the reads before this bad block.

The format of BAM files may vary between different aligners, but featureCounts should be able to process all of them if their formats followed the BAM specification. Can you please try using SAMtools to decompress one of the BAM file that had this problem to see if SAMtools can finish it correctly? If it can correctly decompress the BAM file, can you please count the number of reads in the SAMtools output to see if featureCounts has already processed all these reads? (i.e., is the bad block the last block in the BAM file?) Some aligners can generate BAM files that have the last block damaged if the program terminates unexpectedly.

Thank you for the helps.

Cheers,

Yang

messages.body_plain:
We tried a few different things using the existing BAM files that still returned the same error:
1. Converting BAM to SAM and applying featureCounts
2. Using older versions of featureCounts on the same BAM file

We also counted with htseq which appeared to run successfully, i.e. did not receive any errors although it could have ignored reads with the error present, rather than stop counting for the rest of the chromosome

We lastly regenerated one of the BAM files using TopHat, which did work with featureCounts without any errors, suggesting that there was something wrong somewhere in the BAM file, but the problem seems to elude most sensible samtools checks. We would be willing to share one of the offending BAM files with you so that you can take a look and try to track down exactly what is throwing that error (since you hadn't seen it before)

Thanks,
Andrew

When you converted BAM to SAM and applied featureCounts, did you see the same error message? It has no chance to appear when the input file is a SAM file.

messages.subject: Re: Please describe the featureCounts summary
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kamil and Wei,

On Mon, Feb 2, 2015 at 12:43 PM, Kamil Slowikowski wrote:
> I asked Wei about contributing. This was his reply:
>
> I’m not sure if it is a good idea to allow other people to make
> contributions to our package at the moment since the pacakge includes quite
> a few programs and it has a complexed structure. We might move the code
> repository to for example git-hub in the future, but at this stage we would
> like to keep it to ourselves to ensure a smooth development of the programs
> (especially new programs and algorithms).

Putting the code on GitHub will not hurt the development. Git is a
distributed version control system. Thus no one can make changes to
the main codebase without the approval of the owner of the code
repository. See the link below for how development with distributed
version control systems, e.g. Git, differs from development with
centralized systems like Subversion:

http://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-About-Version-Control

> I believe that source code for scientific software — regardless of
> complexity — should be stored in a permanent public repository that
> encourages contributions from the community.

100% agree.

> You might consider creating a separate github repo with the R package for
> subread.

Bioconductor has support for this. You can allow others to help you
develop the software using Git/GitHub, and you can continue to develop
the software as you have been using Subversion.

http://bioconductor.org/developers/how-to/git-svn/

Subread is a great tool that many users find very useful. Wei, please
consider letting us help you improve it.

Best,

John
